seo_title: NCLAT: Hiding a Decree Debt Justifies CIRP Recall
title: NCLAT New Delhi Upholds Recall of CIRP and Rs 5 Lakh Penalty for Concealing a Decree Debt in a Section 10 Filing
case_name: Intarvo Technologies Private Limited & Anr. v. Vivek Jairath
card_summary: Intarvo Technologies did not disclose a Rs 2.29 crore decree the Saket district court had passed for Vivek Jairath days before its Section 10 filing, admitted by the NCLT on 16 October 2023. The NCLT later recalled the admission under Section 65 and fined Intarvo Rs 5 lakh. NCLAT New Delhi dismissed the appeals, holding the decree was a material liability that should have been disclosed.
card_tip: A corporate debtor filing for voluntary insolvency under Section 10 must disclose every decree it knows of; concealing even a recent district court decree risks recall of the whole CIRP and a Section 65 penalty.
verification_notes: LiveLaw Biz's report and its IBC weekly digest (9-15 November 2026) agree on the bench (Justice Mohd Faiz Alam Khan and Arun Baroka), the appeal numbers, the 30 October 2026 order date, the Section 65 recall and Rs 5 lakh penalty, and the holding on non-disclosure. The IBBI order-process page for Intarvo (CIN U72100DL2001PTC109841) independently confirms the company's 16 October 2023 CIRP admission date and subsequent RP appointment, corroborating the underlying timeline from an official record. The NCLT's original recall order is separately dated 12 June 2025; that is the order under appeal, not the NCLAT decision date used here.
